const screeningRules = [
  'Use only the supplied title, abstract, publication types, and article metadata.',
  'Do not use outside knowledge.',

  'The target plant must be directly investigated or directly evaluated in the review.',

  'Assess whether the clinical efficacy evidence can be specifically attributed to the target plant.',

  'Set plant_specific_efficacy_evidence to true only when the clinical efficacy outcome can be specifically attributed to the target plant.',

  'Set plant_specific_efficacy_evidence to false when the target plant is only one component of a fixed multi-herb combination and no plant-specific effect is reported.',

  'Set plant_specific_efficacy_evidence to false when the target plant is pooled together with other drugs or treatments in one intervention group and no plant-specific result is reported.',

  'Set plant_specific_efficacy_evidence to false when a review only lists or mentions the target plant among many interventions without a plant-specific clinical efficacy conclusion.',

  'A separate treatment arm containing the target plant alone counts as plant-specific evidence.',

  'A systematic review or meta-analysis counts as plant-specific evidence when it reports a clinical efficacy conclusion specifically for the target plant.',

  'Assess how closely the investigated indication matches the target indication.',

  'Do not exclude a clinically relevant paper only because disease severity differs from the target indication.',

  'Use exact_match when the investigated indication and severity clearly match the target indication.',

  'Use partial_overlap when the same clinical condition is investigated but the population, severity, stage, or diagnostic definition differs.',

  'Use related when the study is clinically related but does not directly investigate the target condition.',

  'Use unrelated when the investigated condition is not relevant to the target indication.',

  'Include only human clinical efficacy evidence or systematic reviews/meta-analyses of human clinical efficacy evidence.',

  'Exclude preclinical, animal, in-vitro, pharmacokinetic-only, mechanistic-only, safety-only, or interaction-only papers from efficacy evidence.',

  'Exclude articles where the target plant is only mentioned incidentally.',

  'Use uncertain when the abstract does not provide enough information for a confident decision.',

  'The screening decision must not be interpreted as an efficacy assessment.',

  'supporting_quote must be copied exactly from the supplied title or abstract.',

  'The supporting quote should directly support the screening decision, indication relation, or plant-specific attribution.',

  'If no exact supporting quote exists, use null.'
];

const targetSchema = {
  screening_decision: null,
  indication_relation: null,
  direct_plant_match: null,
  plant_specific_efficacy_evidence: null,
  human_clinical_evidence: null,
  evidence_design: null,
  reason: null,
  supporting_quote: null
};

return {
  json: {
    ...$json,

    screening_config: {
      schema_version: 'phythera_pubmed_screen_v3',
      rules: screeningRules,
      target_schema: targetSchema
    }
  }
};

parameters.text:
=You are screening biomedical literature for PhyThera,
a professional medicinal-plant evidence mapping platform.

TARGET PLANT:
{{ $json.scientific_name }}

TARGET INDICATION:
{{ $json.target_indication }}

PMID:
{{ $json.pmid }}

PUBLICATION TYPES:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.publication_types) }}

TITLE:
{{ $json.title }}

ABSTRACT:
{{ $json.abstract }}

SCREENING RULES:
- {{ $json.screening_config.rules.join('\n- ') }}

TARGET JSON STRUCTURE:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.screening_config.target_schema, null, 2) }}

Allowed screening_decision values:
- include
- exclude
- uncertain

Allowed indication_relation values:
- exact_match
- partial_overlap
- related
- unrelated
- uncertain

Allowed evidence_design values:
- systematic_review_meta_analysis
- systematic_review
- randomized_controlled_trial
- clinical_trial
- other

DECISION LOGIC:

screening_decision = include only when ALL of the following are true:
- direct_plant_match = true
- plant_specific_efficacy_evidence = true
- human_clinical_evidence = true
- indication_relation is exact_match or partial_overlap

screening_decision = exclude when ANY of the following apply:
- direct_plant_match = false
- plant_specific_efficacy_evidence = false
- human_clinical_evidence = false
- indication_relation = unrelated

screening_decision = uncertain when the abstract does not provide enough information to determine one or more essential criteria reliably.

PLANT-SPECIFIC ATTRIBUTION:

Set plant_specific_efficacy_evidence = true only when the reported clinical efficacy result can be specifically attributed to the target plant.

Examples that ARE plant-specific:
- The target plant is administered alone in its own intervention arm.
- The target plant is directly compared with placebo or another treatment.
- A systematic review or meta-analysis reports efficacy results specifically for the target plant.

Examples that are NOT plant-specific:
- The target plant is one ingredient in a fixed multi-herb combination and no separate effect is available.
- The target plant is pooled with other drugs or treatments in a single intervention group.
- A review merely lists the target plant among many interventions without reporting a plant-specific clinical efficacy conclusion.
- The target plant is mentioned only in background information.

INDICATION MATCHING:

- exact_match:
  The target condition and relevant severity clearly match.

- partial_overlap:
  The same clinical condition is studied, but severity, population, stage, or diagnostic definition differs.

- related:
  A clinically related condition is studied, but it is not the target condition itself.

- unrelated:
  The investigated condition is not relevant to the target indication.

A difference in disease severity alone is NOT sufficient for exclusion.

IMPORTANT:
- Do not use outside knowledge.
- Do not infer missing study details.
- Do not infer efficacy from the screening decision.
- Do not determine an Evidence Score.
- Return valid JSON only.
- Do not use Markdown.
- Do not add keys.
- direct_plant_match must be true or false.
- plant_specific_efficacy_evidence must be true or false.
- human_clinical_evidence must be true or false.
- reason must be concise and factual.
- supporting_quote must be one exact contiguous passage from TITLE or ABSTRACT.
- Prefer a quote that directly supports plant-specific attribution and clinical relevance.
- If no exact supporting quote exists, use null.

Return only the JSON object.

const outcomeRules = [
  'Use only the supplied title, abstract, publication types, and article metadata.',
  'Do not use outside knowledge.',
  'Do not infer information that is not explicitly stated in the abstract.',
  'Do not calculate or derive missing numerical values.',
  'Do not sum subgroup sizes to create a total sample size.',
  'Extract only clinical efficacy information relevant to the target indication.',
  'Do not convert screening relevance into an efficacy conclusion.',
  'Preserve negative, neutral, mixed, and positive findings equally.',

  'For randomized trials, describe the target plant intervention separately from comparator treatments.',

  'For systematic reviews or meta-analyses, extract the review-level clinical conclusion rather than pretending the review is a single trial.',

  'Capture named extracts or preparations exactly when stated, for example WS 5570, LI-160, or Calmigen.',

  'If dose or duration is not explicitly reported, use null.',

  'sample_size must only contain a total sample size explicitly stated in the supplied title or abstract.',

  'If only subgroup sizes are reported and no total sample size is explicitly stated, use null.',

  'Mark continuation or follow-up publications separately from primary acute-treatment reports.',

  'If the abstract explicitly identifies an earlier or parent trial, capture that relationship.',

  'Do not guess a parent trial PMID.',

  'outcome_direction describes the direction of the reported clinical efficacy evidence, not study quality, heterogeneity, certainty, or risk of bias.',

  'Use supportive when the reported results support efficacy of the target plant.',

  'A result showing the target plant is superior to placebo counts as supportive.',

  'A result showing the target plant has comparable or similar efficacy to an active established treatment counts as supportive, not mixed.',

  'Non-inferiority or therapeutic equivalence to an active comparator counts as supportive when explicitly reported.',

  'Use not_supportive when the reported results fail to support efficacy of the target plant, show no efficacy versus placebo, or favor the comparator over the target plant.',

  'Use mixed only when efficacy findings themselves are materially conflicting, equivocal, or inconsistent within the article.',

  'Do not use mixed merely because the target plant is superior to placebo but similar to an active comparator.',

  'Do not use mixed merely because heterogeneity, limitations, or uncertainty are reported if the overall efficacy direction remains supportive.',

  'Use unclear when the abstract does not allow a reliable efficacy direction.',

  'supporting_quote must be copied exactly from the supplied title or abstract.',

  'If no exact supporting quote exists, use null.',

  'When placebo is a comparator, lack of a significant efficacy difference versus placebo must take precedence over similarity to an active comparator.',

  'If the article explicitly describes the efficacy findings as equivocal and reports no significant between-treatment difference including placebo, use mixed.',

  'Do not classify an article as supportive solely because the target plant is similar to an active comparator when placebo performs similarly as well.'
];

const targetSchema = {
  publication_role: null,
  study_phase: null,

  population: null,
  sample_size: null,
  indication_as_studied: null,

  intervention: null,
  preparation_or_extract: null,
  dose_regimen: null,

  comparator: null,
  treatment_duration: null,

  primary_efficacy_outcome: null,
  effect_estimate: null,

  outcome_direction: null,
  efficacy_summary: null,

  parent_trial_reference: null,

  supporting_quote: null
};

return {
  json: {
    ...$json,

    outcome_extraction_config: {
      schema_version:
        'phythera_pubmed_outcome_v3',

      rules:
        outcomeRules,

      target_schema:
        targetSchema
    }
  }
};

parameters.text:
=You are extracting structured clinical evidence for PhyThera,
a professional medicinal-plant evidence mapping platform.

Use ONLY the supplied article information.
Do not use outside knowledge.

TARGET PLANT:
{{ $json.scientific_name }}

TARGET INDICATION:
{{ $json.target_indication }}

PMID:
{{ $json.pmid }}

EVIDENCE DESIGN:
{{ $json.screening.evidence_design }}

INDICATION RELATION:
{{ $json.screening.indication_relation }}

PUBLICATION TYPES:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.publication_types) }}

TITLE:
{{ $json.title }}

ABSTRACT:
{{ $json.abstract }}

EXTRACTION RULES:
- {{ $json.outcome_extraction_config.rules.join('\n- ') }}

TARGET JSON STRUCTURE:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.outcome_extraction_config.target_schema, null, 2) }}

ALLOWED VALUES:

publication_role:
- primary_trial_report
- continuation_follow_up_report
- systematic_review_meta_analysis
- systematic_review
- other

study_phase:
- acute_treatment
- continuation
- maintenance
- follow_up
- review_level
- unclear

outcome_direction:
- supportive
- not_supportive
- mixed
- unclear

FIELD DEFINITIONS:

publication_role:
Classify what kind of publication this specific article is.

Use primary_trial_report when this paper reports the main clinical trial results.

Use continuation_follow_up_report when this paper reports continuation,
maintenance, extension, relapse-prevention, or follow-up results from an
earlier or preceding treatment phase.

Use systematic_review_meta_analysis for reviews that quantitatively pool
clinical studies.

Use systematic_review for systematic clinical reviews without a clearly
reported quantitative meta-analysis.

study_phase:
For primary clinical trials, classify the treatment phase.

For continuation or extension papers use continuation, maintenance,
or follow_up as appropriate.

For reviews use review_level.

If unclear use unclear.

population:
Briefly describe the clinical population exactly as supported by the abstract.

Include relevant restrictions such as postmenopausal women when explicitly stated.

sample_size:
Return a total sample size ONLY when the total number is explicitly stated
in the supplied title or abstract.

Do NOT calculate a total by adding treatment groups, subgroups, or study arms.

Example:
If the abstract states:
69 patients received treatment A,
68 received treatment B,
24 received placebo,
but never explicitly states a total sample size,
return null.

Return a number only or null.

indication_as_studied:
Describe the condition actually investigated in the study.

Do not replace it with the PhyThera target indication.

intervention:
Describe the target plant intervention.

preparation_or_extract:
Capture a named preparation, extract, or product exactly when stated,
for example WS 5570, LI-160, or Calmigen.

Otherwise return null.

dose_regimen:
Capture dose and frequency when explicitly stated.

Otherwise return null.

comparator:
Describe placebo, active comparator, usual care, or other comparison groups.

For reviews, summarize the main comparator types when stated.

treatment_duration:
Capture only a treatment duration explicitly stated in the abstract.

Do not calculate duration from dates or treatment phases.

Otherwise return null.

primary_efficacy_outcome:
Identify the main clinically relevant efficacy outcome for the target indication.

Do not use purely mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, or safety outcomes.

effect_estimate:
Capture the most informative numerical efficacy result explicitly reported.

Include effect measure and confidence interval where available.

Do not calculate new statistics.

If no suitable numerical estimate is explicitly provided, return null.

outcome_direction:
Classify the DIRECTION OF CLINICAL EFFICACY RESULTS.

This field does NOT represent:
- study quality
- evidence certainty
- heterogeneity
- risk of bias
- publication bias
- safety
- limitations

supportive:
Use supportive when the reported clinical efficacy findings support the
target plant.

Examples:
- target plant is superior to placebo
- target plant improves the relevant clinical outcome
- target plant has comparable efficacy to an established active treatment
- target plant is reported as therapeutically equivalent or non-inferior
  to an active comparator

IMPORTANT:
Being superior to placebo AND similar to an active antidepressant is SUPPORTIVE,
not mixed.

Study heterogeneity or methodological limitations alone do NOT make an
otherwise supportive result mixed.

not_supportive:
Use not_supportive when the efficacy findings fail to support the target plant.

Examples:
- no significant efficacy versus placebo
- placebo performs similarly or better
- the active comparator clearly outperforms the target plant
- authors explicitly conclude that efficacy was not supported

mixed:
Use mixed only when the EFFICACY FINDINGS THEMSELVES are materially conflicting,
equivocal, or inconsistent.

Examples:
- some clinically relevant efficacy outcomes support the plant while others do not
- different treatment phases produce conflicting results
- the article explicitly describes the efficacy result as equivocal

Do NOT use mixed merely because:
- the plant is superior to placebo but similar to an active comparator
- study heterogeneity is reported
- limitations are reported
- evidence certainty is limited
- more research is recommended

unclear:
Use unclear when the abstract does not contain enough information to determine
the efficacy direction reliably.

efficacy_summary:
Write one concise factual sentence summarizing the reported efficacy findings.

Preserve positive, negative, neutral, and equivocal findings faithfully.

parent_trial_reference:
Use this only for continuation, maintenance, extension, or follow-up publications.

Capture an exact textual description of the earlier or parent trial when the
abstract provides one.

Do NOT invent a PMID, DOI, trial identifier, or citation.

Otherwise return null.

supporting_quote:
Copy one exact contiguous passage from TITLE or ABSTRACT that best supports
the efficacy conclusion and outcome_direction.

Do not paraphrase the quote.

If no suitable exact quote exists, return null.

OUTPUT RULES:
- Return valid JSON only.
- Do not use Markdown.
- Do not add keys.
- Do not calculate missing values.
- Do not infer information not explicitly supported by the supplied article.
- sample_size must be a number or null.
- All other missing values must be null.
- supporting_quote must be copied exactly from TITLE or ABSTRACT.

Return only the JSON object.
